pluginPurpose: zz-core owns the record every flow writes into: identity, documents, gates, knowledge and telemetry, and what anybody reports broken. This protocol measures whether zz-core actually holds up that record so a decision a team made once stays durable, findable, and gated before anything downstream depends on it. It is the initiative's bootstrap reference protocol (FR-57, spec v8): sufficient to validate the architecture end to end, not a claim about zz-core's real quality — scoring.establishment.bootstrap=true keeps every run at best provisional until the first real post-close OBSERVE/DISCOVER cycle.

anchors.text:
# Spec: export a team's decisions as CSV

## Problem
Team leads copy decisions out of the knowledge store by hand every month; it takes an hour and misses entries.

## Scope
In: one CSV export per team, from the console. Out: scheduling, other formats.

## Requirements
FR-1 The export holds every approved decision with its date, title and initiative.
FR-2 Only members of the team may export it.

## Acceptance criteria
AC-1 Exporting a team with 3 approved decisions yields a CSV of 3 rows plus a header.
AC-2 A non-member's export request is refused with 403.

anchors.text: Decision: gated documents are stored in Postgres, not as files on disk. Why: in 0.40 two writers raced on the file lock and one approval was lost; Postgres row locks serialise them. Applies to: any tool that writes or approves a gated document.
